_about: Manifest for the measured-plant fixtures. Every number in host/pico_esc/measured.py traces to a
file listed here, and every file records which MECHANICAL CONFIGURATION and which ESC cross_up it
was recorded at — the two things that were previously implicit and got mixed.

_cross_up_provenance.claim: prop_350kv_20260726 datasets are cross_up=34; bare_shaft_350kv_20260730 are cross_up=36
why_it_needed_evidence: No fixture CSV carries a cross_up column (only duty_sweep.py stamps one, into its own output).
Git history looked like it said 36 for BOTH: the bench was recalibrated at cross_up=36 on
2026-07-26 17:46 (commit 011acf8), the prop-on dynamics dataset was committed 2026-07-27 00:17
(235eb56) with no reflash commit in between, the 2026-07-29 session note records cross_up=36 and
evidence: Two no-load duty sweeps recorded minutes apart at the two values: reports/duty_sweep_20260729_220535.csv
(A) and reports/duty_sweep_20260729_223122.csv (B). They are offset by EXACTLY 30 command counts at
every point (A: 780->2922.2, 570->753.2; B: 750->2932.2, 540->768.9) — a pure intercept shift, which
is what cross_rescale_duty does, and independent confirmation that cross_up moves the intercept and
Which sweep is which, pinned against a KNOWN cross_up rather than by assuming the sign: the ESC was
read directly and reports sine_cross_up: 36; at cmd 600 the encoder measured 1064.3 and 1069.3 rpm on
two independent runs. Sweep A interpolates to 1072.8 there (0.4-0.8 % away), sweep B to 1391.7 (30 %
away, far beyond any load effect - today is bare shaft and sweep A was prop-on). So A = 36, B = 34.
Interpolating both sweeps to the postfix sysid's three 6-step commands: measured 794.4 / 1510.4 /
cmd 680 against a directly-measured sweep whose own cross_up is pinned by a known-configuration
reconciliation_with_git: esctool.py flash WIPES the ESC config to firmware defaults and must be followed by re-applying the
whole config (a documented, recurring gotcha in this project). A flash between the 17:46 velcal and
the 00:17 sysid leaves NO commit trace, which is exactly why no reflash is visible in history. The
velcal commit message describes the config velcal ran under; the sysid that followed sat at the
also_derived: The 30-count offset over 2 cross_up units gives K = 0.00265*30/2 = 0.0398 duty/unit, between the
code's DUTY6_CROSSUP_K = 0.0421 and the theoretical 0.0391 — so the sign AND magnitude of the
existing term are sound. Sign convention (host/pico_esc/motor_model.py:duty6): a HIGHER cross_up

_open_loop_commands.note: Inferred from each tool's default/documented invocation, NOT recorded in the CSVs. Flagged.
_open_loop_commands.steptrace_startup2400: rpm 2400 from rest (closed loop, --mode rpm --startup); ABORT_STALLs

sinesweep_noprop_20260730_033014.csv.note: cmd 60..600 step 30, both legs. Source of TELE_FLOOR_MECH, SINE_SPREAD_TABLE_BARE, SINE_REVERSALS_BARE and the bare-shaft static points at cmd 570/600.

sinesweep_fold_noprop_20260730_033417.cs.note: fine sweep cmd 495..555 through the seam. Departure bracket 515..520 on BOTH legs — no hysteresis resolved. Source of the cmd 555 static point.

coastdown_noprop_20260730_032130.csv.note: 3 repeats of the zero-throttle brake. Source of L_PHASE_FITTED, J_BARE_FITTED and FREE_DECEL_BARE_RPM_S.

cutmode_noprop_20260730_032448.csv.note: NO `run` column — the key column is `mode`, which is why coastdown.py --analyze had to learn both. Source of CUT_RELEASE_S and BRAKE_ENGAGE_S. brake_on_stop=0 does not disable any of the three.

coastdown_20260730_011123.csv.note: PROPELLER FITTED. Held out of the brake fit, so replaying it with the bare-shaft-fitted L and the prop-on J/drag is the genuine out-of-sample check. Also the source of J_PROP.

steptrace_down_noprop_20260730_033706.cs.trim: TIME-trimmed to the first 2.0 s per run; NOT decimated
steptrace_down_noprop_20260730_033706.cs.note: The half-time is 22-26 ms, i.e. ~5 samples, so decimating this file would destroy the one number it exists to measure. Source of SINE_PULLOUT_NM.

steptrace_startup2400_noprop_20260730_03.trim: time-trimmed to 4.0 s per run, then decimated 2x
